evals.name: migration-minhphat-full-discovery
evals.prompt: Minh Phat Retail wants to move their SQL Server data warehouse to Databricks. I have a sources/ folder with DDL, stored procedures, one SSIS package, one SSRS report, SQL Agent exports, Query Store output, SSRS logs, row counts, a 2016 spec, kickoff notes and one DBA interview transcript. Help me run discovery & assessment: identify the project type, check whether the inputs are sufficient, extract requirements and business rules, and give me a draft assessment with the list of questions to ask the client.
evals.expected_output: Intake with 3 axes, source request, sufficiency table, registers with locators, rationalization draft, ≤5 blocking questions, no fabricated inventory or Lakebridge output.
assertions: Classifies the project as migration/modernization AND identifies the REAL driver as the SQL Server license ending Dec 2026 (not 'modernization'), with performance/nightly window as secondary
States the Axis C decision explicitly: CTO decides wave-1 scope and budget by 2026-10-15 (from kickoff notes slide 5)
Records input levels per source: L2/L3 for MP_DWH (code + Query Store + job exports), and notes SAP PO and POS source system are L0 (no export) — does not treat them as known
Does NOT claim 340 tables / 87 procedures / 23 SSIS as inventory facts; notes the fixture contains 15 DDL, 6 procs, 1 SSIS, 1 SSRS and that slide 9's counts are unverified
Does NOT fabricate Lakebridge Analyzer output or complexity tiers; states the Analyzer was not run and recommends running it (`databricks labs lakebridge analyze`)

Extracts the HCM-99 exclusion, status<>9 exclusion, and 7-day return window from sp_Calc_Daily_Revenue with code locators, and marks them CODE-ONLY or CONFLICT against spec 2016 §4.1 (which says returns are subtracted on processing day)

Identifies the MIN_TXN_AMOUNT conflict: spec §4.2 says 5,000; code reads CFG_PARAM; dump shows 10,000 changed 2021 by nguyen.t — marked CONFLICT and CONFIG-ONLY, with an open question, NOT resolved unilaterally
Flags the INNER JOIN to DIM_STORE in sp_Calc_Daily_Revenue as silent data loss (finding), and notes the SSIS Lookup Store IgnoreFailure inconsistency
Identifies TEST-01 exclusion (spec §4.3) as DOC-ONLY / not in code, and that the SSRS report applies region<>'TEST' filter and net_amt_adj zeroing (<5 txns) as report-level business rules
Identifies Loyalty points (spec §6) as DOC-ONLY: RPT_LOYALTY_POINTS has 0 rows, 0 reads, 0 report executions, DBA confirms never built
Does NOT call FACT_YEAREND_INVENTORY orphan: recognises JOB_YEAREND yearly schedule (freq_type 32), 6 reads, last 2026-01-05, and DBA statement at 00:38:20
Does NOT call TMP_REV_2019_BACKUP orphan despite its name: recognises JOB_MONTHEND_CLOSE writes it monthly and it has 12 reads / last read 2026-09-01

Identifies ARCH_POS_TXN_2015 and OLD_CUSTOMER_IMPORT as retire candidates with usage evidence (0 reads in 396-day Query Store window), and sp_Archive_Txn_2015 as DEAD/unscheduled — while stating that retire requires owner confirmation

Flags sp_Rebuild_Customer_Segment as critical-path / modernize: TRUNCATE + cursor full rebuild ~4h (step 4 in job history) for ~50k daily changes; and notes the CONFLICT that spec §5 says monthly while the job runs daily
Notes segment thresholds are hard-coded (10/1) while CFG_PARAM has SEGMENT_VIP_THRESHOLD=10 that the proc does not read (config not wired) — as a finding or question
Captures sp_Load_POS_Txn rules: linked server [POSSRV01] dependency, DATEADD(hour,7) timezone conversion, UPPER/TRIM on store_cd
Flags sp_Apply_Promo mutating STG_POS_TXN.amount in place before revenue calc (contradicting its own comment) and the Excel-based promo upload as shadow ETL / finding

Security findings: hard-coded svc_etl password in pkg_pos_load.dtsx (ProtectionLevel 0), single shared account for all jobs, CCCD/phone in clear text readable by all logins — and maps them to SEC- requirements
Identifies external consumers from the interview: Finance Excel via ODBC on FACT_DAILY_REVENUE with manual adjustments, and a vendor pulling STG_SAP_PO nightly
Uses the 396-day Query Store window (covers month/quarter/year-end) for usage conclusions and notes that dm_exec stats would only cover since the 2026-09-01 restart

Does NOT turn 'real-time dashboard' (slide 7) into a latency NFR; instead raises a question about what action needs sub-15-minute data; and records the 08:00 (spec) vs 07:00 (Finance now) freshness CONFLICT
Every business rule / requirement / finding presented carries a locator (file:line, §section, or transcript timestamp); no numbers without a source
Open questions name a person or role (e.g. Head of Accounting, Finance, Anh Tuấn/DBA), include a default and impact, and the user is given at most 3–5 blocking questions in the main response

Produces the register files (requirements.jsonl / business_rules.jsonl / inventory.jsonl / findings.jsonl / open_questions.jsonl, or clearly equivalent structured output) plus a sufficiency table showing what cannot be concluded (e.g. POS data quality without source access, effort without Lakebridge trial)
Does not invent Unity Catalog / Databricks object names as if they exist; any target names are explicit placeholders like <catalog>.silver.transactions

Generates the human deliverables from the registers — a single discovery-<project>.xlsx workbook and one assessment-report.md (plus .docx if pandoc) — and does NOT hand-write a second, parallel report
Does not copy the input source files into the output tree; references them by path and sha256 in manifest.json

evals.name: vague-first-ask
evals.prompt: Our client wants to move to Databricks. Where do we start?
evals.expected_output: A provisional classification, a source request and ≤ 5 questions with defaults — no fabricated inventory, no request for 'more information'.
assertions: Classifies provisionally (migration, marked provisional) and says the evidence level is L0
Proposes an Axis C sentence for the user to edit
Emits a source request with required/recommended tiers and why each is needed
Asks at most 5 questions, each with why and a recommended default
Does not answer 'give me more information' and invents no system, table or number

evals.name: cost-performance-not-migration
evals.prompt: Our Databricks bill went up 40% in two quarters and the nightly jobs now overrun. The CFO wants to know why before the budget review. What do we look at first?
evals.expected_output: Classified as cost & performance (not migration); the cost-performance module drives the source request; workspace evidence (system tables) is requested, not invented.
assertions: Classifies the project as cost & performance, with the CFO's budget review as the real driver
Loads the cost-performance module, not the migration one
Requests system-table evidence (billing/usage, job run history) and says it needs a connected workspace
Names no cause of the cost rise before evidence
Proposes an Axis C sentence naming the CFO and the budget review

evals.name: multi-turn-answers-applied
evals.prompt: Earlier in this conversation you asked: (1) the decision the assessment serves, (2) whether Query Store is available, (3) who owns revenue rules. My answers: (1) the CTO decides wave-1 scope and budget by 2026-10-15; (2) yes — the export is in sources/exports/querystore_table_reads_396d.csv; (3) the finance lead, Ms. Lan. Continue the discovery.
evals.expected_output: The answers become records: Axis C updated, the Query Store window used for usage (with its window recorded), revenue-rule questions addressed to the finance lead — and the same questions not asked again.
assertions: Writes the Axis C sentence with the CTO, wave-1 scope and budget, 2026-10-15
Uses the Query Store export as the usage source and records its window in sufficiency.md
Addresses revenue-rule open questions to the finance lead
Does not re-ask any of the three answered questions

evals.name: vietnamese-member
evals.prompt: Khách hàng Minh Phát muốn chuyển kho dữ liệu SQL Server lên Databricks. Thư mục sources/ có DDL, stored procedure và ghi chú kickoff. Giúp tôi bắt đầu discovery.
evals.expected_output: The intake, the questions and every artifact in Vietnamese; identifiers, object names and code verbatim.
assertions: intake.md, the source request and the questions are written in Vietnamese
Object names (sp_Calc_Daily_Revenue, FACT_DAILY_REVENUE) and code stay verbatim
Classifies the project as migration with the license end as the real driver
Asks at most 5 questions
